paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. In this law, the LORD makes room for every woman who walks in, whether she's rich or not. Whatever the baby was, a son or a daughter, one road led back to the Tent of Meeting, and the priest made atonement for her (Leviticus 12:6-7). The LORD is the One who set up that way back in, and He's the One who held it open.

Now look at that last verse, because I almost dropped my spatula. "But if she cannot afford a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons…" (Leviticus 12:8). Then the priest makes atonement for her, and the text says, "she will be clean." I got bought for a QUARTER, so I know what it's like to be the cheap one, and the LORD didn't make a cheaper deal here. Same atonement, same word, clean.

So here's what I'm taking out of the oven. Coming to the LORD was never meant to be a bill only some people could pay. He had said, "…be holy, because I am holy" (Leviticus 11:45), and in this passage He shows how a person gets close to that holiness: through the offering and the priest's atonement, not by how much she brought. So if you ever feel like you showed up with less than everybody else, remember that verse. He made a way for the one with the lamb and the one with the pigeons.
